## Purpose and execution model
nanochat is a minimal end-to-end experimental harness for training and serving small GPT-style LLMs on a single node, scaling from CPU/MPS to multi-GPU CUDA. It covers tokenizer training, base pretraining, supervised chat finetuning, RL, evaluation, and CLI inference. The main reproducible pipeline is `runs/speedrun.sh`; primary Python entry points are `scripts/base_train.py`, `scripts/chat_sft.py`, `scripts/chat_rl.py`, and `scripts/chat_cli.py`.

## Model and precision core
The Transformer implementation is concentrated in `nanochat/gpt.py`, with attention acceleration/fallback behavior in `nanochat/flash_attention.py`. Global hardware-aware compute dtype selection is centralized in `nanochat/common.py`: weights remain fp32 for optimization while forward paths explicitly use the selected compute dtype, rather than `torch.amp.autocast`. Optional FP8 support is isolated in `nanochat/fp8.py`.

## Pretraining data and tokenization
Pretraining consumes downloadable/readable dataset shards through `nanochat/dataset.py`, then tokenizes and distributes batches via `nanochat/dataloader.py`. The BPE tokenizer abstraction, including chat rendering, is in `nanochat/tokenizer.py`; it is produced and assessed by `scripts/tok_train.py` and `scripts/tok_eval.py`. Reference shard generation is an offline developer process in `dev/repackage_data_reference.py`.

## Training orchestration and scaling contract
`scripts/base_train.py` is the central training loop. Its defining interface is model `--depth`: the repository derives architecture and training hyperparameters to produce compute-optimal model variants rather than exposing a broad configuration system. It runs standalone or under `torchrun`, with distributed execution and gradient accumulation adapting to available GPU count. Optimization—including AdamW/Muon and distributed variants—is owned by `nanochat/optim.py`; checkpoint persistence/resume is handled by `nanochat/checkpoint_manager.py`.

## Evaluation and experiment feedback
Base-model evaluation is coordinated by `scripts/base_eval.py`, using bits-per-byte loss evaluation from `nanochat/loss_eval.py` and the DCLM CORE metric implementation in `nanochat/core_eval.py`. The speedrun optimizes time to exceed GPT-2’s CORE score. `runs/miniseries.sh` and `runs/scaling_laws.sh` launch depth sweeps and research experiments; training can report metrics to Weights & Biases.

## Chat post-training and task boundary
Chat SFT and RL are distinct stages invoked by `scripts/chat_sft.py` and `scripts/chat_rl.py`. Evaluation tasks are modularized under `tasks/`, with task composition in `tasks/common.py` and benchmark/data adapters such as `tasks/arc.py`, `tasks/gsm8k.py`, `tasks/mmlu.py`, and Hugging Face SmolTalk integration in `tasks/smoltalk.py`. `scripts/chat_eval.py` evaluates post-trained chat models against these task abstractions.

## Inference and tool execution
`nanochat/engine.py` provides efficient autoregressive inference with a KV cache, used by interactive serving in `scripts/chat_cli.py` and performance measurement in `scripts/infer_bench.py`. The optional model-to-tool boundary is explicit: `nanochat/execution.py` enables sandboxed Python execution, rather than embedding tool logic inside the model or task layers.

## Runtime and external dependencies
The primary runtime is Python/PyTorch, managed with uv (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`). CUDA A100/H100 multi-GPU nodes are the performance target, while CPU and Apple MPS are supported through the same code paths (`runs/runcpu.sh`). External services/data include Hugging Face-hosted datasets, Weights & Biases experiment tracking, and cloud GPU providers as deployment infrastructure rather than required application services.
